name: Old Age Pension
full_name: Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme (Tamil Nadu)
summary: A monthly pension for destitute people aged 60 and over.
benefit_note: ₹1,200 a month. For ages 60 to 79 this is ₹200 from the centre and ₹1,000 from the state; from 80 it is ₹500 and ₹700.
how_to_apply: Apply at your Village Administrative Officer, Gram Panchayat or Urban Local Body office.
The Revenue Department verifies your circumstances.
Once approved, the pension is credited to your bank account each month.

TRANSLATION WARNING. The amounts come from the TAMIL version of the Commissionerate of Revenue Administration page (cra.tn.gov.in/about_schemes_t.php), read through automatic translation on 2026-08-09. The English page 404s. A Tamil reader must check these figures directly — this is the weakest sourcing in the corpus.

Eligibility wording is cross-checked against an official district portal (karur.nic.in social security schemes), which gives the same three conditions: 60 years and above, destitute, below poverty line.

LEVEL IS SET TO STATE, not central, even though this is a centrally co-sponsored scheme. The ₹1,200 figure is the Tamil Nadu combined rate including the state top-up, so the file describes the Tamil Nadu version. Revisit if the corpus ever covers another state.

TO CONFIRM: whether is_bpl should instead be derived from ration_card_type. AAY and PHH cards indicate below poverty line status in Tamil Nadu, so asking a separate question may be redundant — but the mapping is not certain enough to hard-code.
